enzyme_name: Sterol 24-C-methyltransferase (Erg6 / SmtA)
organism_context: Fungi; in Aspergillus fumigatus and A. flavus Erg6 methylates lanosterol to eburicol (in yeast the preferred substrate is zymosterol)
rationale: Erg6 is a single-activity SAM-dependent sterol C-24 methyltransferase; the Aspergillus enzyme performs exactly the lanosterol to eburicol methylation of this entry and no second catalytic activity is reported for it.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-methylation releasing SAH is effectively irreversible left-to-right; ModelSEED's '<' would demethylate eburicol with SAH, which Erg6 does not do.

enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
rationale: The ModelSEED entry reduces to 'UTP = UDP' with no other species, and the pinned snapshot flags status MI:O:-3/P:-1, i.e. exactly one PO3 missing: the Rhea half-reaction's phosphoryl carrier (a protein phospho-histidine or a polyphosphate chain) was dropped because ModelSEED has no compound for it, so no enzyme can honestly be assigned to the equation as written.
direction_note: With the phosphoryl donor/acceptor absent this is not a reaction, so neither '<' nor '>' describes anything an enzyme does.

enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
rationale: Same artifact as rxn53888: 'CTP = CDP' alone, snapshot status MI:O:-3/P:-1, one PO3 unaccounted for because the Rhea half-reaction's phospho-carrier was not mapped; Rhea 55404/55408/55412 are a consecutive UDP/CDP/GDP triplet of one enzyme's half-reactions.
direction_note: Direction is undefined for a half-reaction whose phosphoryl partner is missing.

enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
rationale: 'GTP = GDP' with nothing else; snapshot status MI:H:-1/O:-3/P:-1 confirms a whole phosphoryl group is missing. MetaCyc RXN-20670 and its neighbour RXN-20671 (rxn54354) belong to one phosphotransferase whose phospho-carrier ModelSEED could not represent.
direction_note: Direction is undefined for a half-reaction whose phosphoryl partner is missing.

enzyme_name: 2-amino-2-deoxyisochorismate (ADIC) synthase, PhzE (MST-family chorismate-utilising enzyme)
organism_context: Phenazine-producing Pseudomonas and Burkholderia; the homologous anthranilate synthase is split into separate TrpE and TrpG chains in many bacteria, so the fusion is lineage-specific
rationale: PhzE is one polypeptide carrying an N-terminal MST (ADIC synthase) domain and a C-terminal glutamine amidotransferase domain connected by a substrate-induced ammonia channel, i.e. two genuine catalytic activities on one chain rather than an associating complex.
direction_note: The physiological reaction consumes L-glutamine, hydrolysed by the fused GATase domain and channelled as NH3; that coupling is what makes ADIC formation irreversible forward and it is invisible in the free-ammonia equation ModelSEED holds, which is why the near-zero measured dG pushed ModelSEED the wrong way.

enzyme_name: NcmP, carboxylate O-methyltransferase of the nocamycin pathway
organism_context: Saccharothrix syringae NRRL B-16468 (nocamycin biosynthetic gene cluster)
rationale: Deletion of ncmP accumulates nocamycin E and the recombinant protein was characterised as a SAM-dependent carboxylate O-methyltransferase producing nocamycin I; a single tailoring methylation activity with no second catalytic function reported.
direction_note: A biosynthetic SAM-dependent methyl esterification runs forward; ModelSEED's '<' would demethylate the pathway end-product back to the shunt intermediate.

enzyme_name: EqxD, equisetin N-methyltransferase
organism_context: Fusarium heterosporum ATCC 74349 (eqx cluster); the homologous silent cluster in F. fujikuroi lacks eqxD and therefore stops at trichosetin
rationale: Trichosetin is the N-desmethyl congener of equisetin, and the F. fujikuroi cluster differs from the F. heterosporum eqx cluster precisely by the absence of the N-methyltransferase gene eqxD, assigning this methylation to a stand-alone SAM-dependent methyltransferase.
direction_note: SAM to SAH methyl transfer onto the tetramic acid nitrogen is a committed biosynthetic step, not a reversible one.

enzyme_name: unidentified phosphotransferase (phosphoryl partner lost on import)
rationale: 'ADP = AMP' with nothing else; snapshot status MI:O:-3/P:-1 shows one PO3 missing. MetaCyc RXN-20671 sits next to RXN-20670 (the GDP/GTP entry), so both are half-reactions of one phosphotransferase whose phospho-carrier ModelSEED dropped.
direction_note: Direction is undefined for a half-reaction whose phosphoryl partner is missing.

enzyme_name: 12-oxophytodienoate reductase OPR2 / OPR3 (Old Yellow Enzyme family ene-reductase)
organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis thaliana, Solanum lycopersicum); the OPR3-independent jasmonate route
rationale: Chini et al. showed 4,5-didehydrojasmonate is reduced to jasmonic acid by OPR2 (and OPR3), FMN-dependent OYE-family ene-reductases with a single C=C reduction activity; the flavin is a tightly bound prosthetic group, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: NADPH-driven flavin ene-reduction is effectively irreversible; no OPR oxidises jasmonate back to 4,5-didehydrojasmonate, so ModelSEED's '<' is the wrong sense.

enzyme_name: FbiB (F420-0:gamma-glutamyl ligase with C-terminal FMN-dependent dehydro-F420-0 reductase domain)
distinct_activities: FMNH2-dependent dehydro-F420-0 reductase (C-terminal FMN-binding nitroreductase-like domain)
organism_context: Mycobacterium smegmatis and M. tuberculosis and other F420-producing actinobacteria; in Thermomicrobia the reductase is a stand-alone nitroreductase-superfamily protein
rationale: Bashiri et al. showed the C-terminal domain of FbiB uses FMNH2 to reduce dehydro-F420-0 to F420-0 while the N-terminal domain is the gamma-glutamyl ligase, so one polypeptide carries two distinct catalytic activities.
direction_note: The documented reaction is FMNH2 + dehydro-F420-0 -> FMN + F420-0, which is right-to-left as ModelSEED writes the entry; ModelSEED's '<' is therefore the correct direction and the council's '>' would run the maturation step backwards.

enzyme_name: Human UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A3, with UGT2B7/UGT1A10 contributing)
organism_context: Human liver and intestine; ER-membrane UGT1A/2B family
rationale: UGT1A3 is the principal human UGT glucuronidating candesartan (characterised as highly selective for the tetrazole N2, with the acyl/O-glucuronide also formed); UGTs are single-activity glycosyltransferases, and homo/hetero-oligomerisation is not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: Glucuronyl transfer from UDP-glucuronate with UDP release is a committed conjugation step; ModelSEED's '<' would have UDP plus the glucuronide regenerate UDP-glucuronate, which no UGT does.

enzyme_name: Human UDP-glucuronosyltransferase UGT1A3
organism_context: Human liver and intestine; zolasartan (zolarsartan) is one of the sartans assayed with recombinant UGT1A3
rationale: Alonen et al. showed recombinant UGT1A3 glucuronidates losartan, candesartan and zolarsartan; UGT1A3 is a single-activity membrane glycosyltransferase with no second catalytic function.
direction_note: UDP-glucuronate-dependent conjugation is effectively irreversible forward, so the ModelSEED '<' is the wrong sense.

enzyme_name: MelA, aspulvinone E synthetase (NRPS-like aryl alpha-keto acid dimerising synthetase)
distinct_activities: furanone-forming thioesterase (TE) domain: Claisen-type C-C condensation and cyclisation
organism_context: Aspergillus terreus; the same A-T-TE architecture with a quinone-forming TE gives atromentin synthetases
rationale: MelA is a single-chain NRPS-like enzyme that non-oxidatively homodimerises 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate; two catalytic domains sit on the one polypeptide (adenylation, and a furanone-forming TE whose catalytic triad cysteine was shown to be essential), while the T domain is a carrier, not a catalyst.
direction_note: The snapshot flags MI:C:-1/H:-1/O:-2 - the one-carbon leaving group lost in forming the C17 butenolide is missing, and the 2 ATP consumed by the adenylation domain are absent too, so the stored dG that drove ModelSEED to '<' is computed on an equation that is not the enzyme's reaction; the biosynthetic sense is nevertheless condensation (left-to-right).

enzyme_name: unidentified fungal dioxolanone synthetase (phenylpyruvate homodimerisation)
organism_context: Guignardia (Phyllosticta) bidwellii, the grape black-rot pathogen, which secretes phenguignardic and guignardic acid as phytotoxins
rationale: Phenguignardic acid is a dioxolanone formed by dimerisation of two phenylpyruvate units derived from phenylalanine, but I found no publication naming or characterising the protein that makes it, so the catalyst and its domain content are genuinely unknown; by analogy to the NRPS-like aryl alpha-keto acid synthetases it would be multidomain, but that is inference, not evidence.
direction_note: Phenguignardate is a secreted end-product, so the condensation direction is the biological one; no enzyme is known that cleaves a dioxolanone back to two phenylpyruvates. If the catalyst is NRPS-like, ATP is also missing from this equation.

enzyme_name: Atromentin synthetase (NRPS-like quinone synthetase; AtrA / GreA / InvA1 type)
distinct_activities: quinone-forming thioesterase (TE) domain: Claisen-type C-C condensation and cyclisation
organism_context: Basidiomycetes (Paxillus involutus, Suillus grevillei, Hapalopilus, Tapinella) and Aspergillus section Nigri; polyporic acid and atromentin synthetases evolved independently but share the mechanism
rationale: Atromentin synthetases are single-chain NRPS-like A-T-TE proteins that non-oxidatively homodimerise 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate; the adenylation domain and the quinone-forming thioesterase domain are two distinct catalytic activities on the one polypeptide, and swapping only the TE domain changes the product class.
direction_note: The 2 ATP hydrolysed to AMP + diphosphate by the adenylation domain are absent from the ModelSEED equation; that is the energy coupling which makes the condensation irreversible, so a dG computed without it pushed ModelSEED to the wrong direction.

enzyme_name: MftD, mycofactocin-biosynthesis FMN-dependent oxidative deaminase (lactate-oxidase family)
organism_context: Mycobacterium smegmatis mc2155 and other mycobacteria/actinobacteria carrying mftABCDEF
rationale: MftD catalyses the oxidative deamination of AHDP to pre-mycofactocin and is a single-activity FMN-dependent oxidase; this ModelSEED entry is only the second half of that transformation, the hydrolysis of the C-3 imine, which in flavin oxidative deaminations is normally spontaneous rather than separately catalysed.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of an imine to the ketone with ammonia release is effectively irreversible in water; ModelSEED's '<' would condense free NH3 onto pre-mycofactocin, undoing the step that creates the cofactor's redox centre.

enzyme_name: 1-testosterone hydratase/dehydrogenase (AtcABC molybdoenzyme)
distinct_activities: 1-testosterone hydratase: water addition across the delta-1 bond at C-1
1-hydroxy-steroid dehydrogenase: C-1 oxidation toward the ring-A 1,3-diketone
organism_context: Steroidobacter denitrificans and Thauera spp.; 2,3-seco pathway of anaerobic androgen degradation, atcA is the pathway's marker gene
rationale: Yang et al. isolated and characterised the 'bifunctional 1-testosterone hydratase/dehydrogenase', the molybdoenzyme essential for anaerobic steroid A-ring degradation; it is a multi-subunit complex, but the two activities are attributed to the one catalytic molybdopterin subunit rather than to separate associating chains, and the substrate assignment here is inferred from the pathway chemistry.
direction_note: This is the bifunctionality-explains-the-conflict case: the hydratase half adds water to 1-testosterone and is immediately pulled forward by the dehydrogenase half en route to androstane-1,3,17-trione and the beta-diketone ring-A hydrolase, so the hydration sense (the council's '>') is physiological and ModelSEED's dehydration '<' is not.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous thermal [1,7]-sigmatropic hydrogen shift
organism_context: Vertebrate skin after UVB photolysis of 7-dehydrocholesterol; also occurs in vitro and in foods
rationale: The previtamin D3 to vitamin D3 conversion is a non-enzymatic thermal isomerisation, accelerated by the membrane environment or by beta-cyclodextrin complexation but not by any protein; 'unknown' is used because there is no catalysing enzyme to classify, not because one could not be found.
direction_note: The isomerisation is a temperature-dependent equilibrium, but at body temperature in membranes it lies strongly on the vitamin D3 side and is pulled further by export and DBP binding, so the net direction is previtamin D3 to vitamin D3, the opposite of ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: Human cytosolic sulfotransferase SULT1A1 (SULT1E1 also active on bisphenol A)
organism_context: Human liver and intestine; bisphenol A is a standard substrate of the phenol-sulfating cytosolic SULTs
rationale: Bisphenol A phenolic sulfation is carried out by cytosolic SULT1 enzymes, single-activity PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases; the obligate homodimer is two copies of the same chain, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Sulfuryl transfer from PAPS with release of PAP is effectively irreversible forward; ModelSEED's '<' would resynthesise PAPS from PAP and an aryl sulfate, which SULTs do not do.

enzyme_name: NvfJ, methyltransferase of the novofumigatonin pathway (carboxyl methyl esterification)
organism_context: Aspergillus novofumigatus, nvf cluster; DMOA-derived meroterpenoid biosynthesis
rationale: Matsuda et al. placed NvfJ as the methyl esterifying methyltransferase acting after cyclisation; in the branch where methylation precedes Baeyer-Villiger oxidation, chermesin D is methylated to its methyl ester by NvfJ. A single SAM-dependent methyl transfer, with the methyl group serving as a carboxylate protecting group.
direction_note: A pathway-committed methyl esterification runs forward; ModelSEED's '<' would demethylate and expose the beta-keto acid the methylation exists to protect.

enzyme_name: NvfJ, methyltransferase of the novofumigatonin pathway (carboxyl methyl esterification)
organism_context: Aspergillus novofumigatus, nvf cluster; the nvfJ deletion strain accumulates asnovolin I, identifying it as the NvfJ substrate
rationale: In the main branch, chermesin D is Baeyer-Villiger oxidised to asnovolin I, which NvfJ then methylates to asnovolin K before NvfM reduces the enoyl bond; a single SAM-dependent methyltransferase activity.
direction_note: SAM to SAH methyl ester formation is the committed forward step of this branch, the opposite of ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: unidentified dipeptidase acting on L-alanyl-L-cysteine
rationale: No publication tied a named peptidase to L-alanyl-L-cysteine; any of several broad-specificity cytosolic dipeptidases (CNDP2-, PepD- or PepV-type metallopeptidases) could do it, so naming one would be fabrication.
direction_note: Only hydrolysis is thermodynamically accessible as written; the ModelSEED '<' direction would condense free L-alanine and L-cysteine into a peptide bond with no ATP in the equation, which no enzyme does.

enzyme_name: Bile acid 7alpha-sulfotransferase (cytosolic SULT2A family; mouse Sult2a8 / mL-STL)
organism_context: Mouse liver Sult2a8 is the characterised 7alpha-hydroxyl-preferring bile acid sulfotransferase; the human bile salt sulfotransferase SULT2A1 sulfates mainly at 3alpha, with 7-sulfates as minor products
rationale: Feng et al. identified Sult2a8 as a PPARalpha-regulated cytosolic sulfotransferase preferring the 7alpha-hydroxyl of bile acids, which is the activity this entry needs; cytosolic SULTs are single-activity PAPS-dependent transferases.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is effectively irreversible forward; ModelSEED's '<' would regenerate PAPS from PAP and a bile acid sulfate.

enzyme_name: Bile acid 7alpha-sulfotransferase (cytosolic SULT2A family; mouse Sult2a8 / mL-STL)
organism_context: Mouse liver (Sult2a8); taurine-conjugated cholate is within the 7alpha-hydroxyl substrate preference described for this enzyme
rationale: Same enzyme class as rxn56344: a cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase with a single catalytic activity, acting on the 7alpha-hydroxyl of a conjugated bile acid.
direction_note: Sulfoconjugation runs forward; the reverse is not a sulfotransferase reaction.

enzyme_name: Bile acid 7alpha-sulfotransferase (cytosolic SULT2A family; mouse Sult2a8 / mL-STL)
organism_context: Mouse liver (Sult2a8); taurochenodeoxycholate is a 7alpha-hydroxy conjugated bile acid of the preferred class
rationale: Same enzyme class as rxn56344/rxn56345; a single-activity cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase. Classical work on chenodeoxycholate conjugates found 3-sulfate as the major and 7-sulfate as a minor enzymatic product, consistent with a distinct 7alpha-preferring isoform.
direction_note: Sulfoconjugation runs forward; the reverse is not a sulfotransferase reaction.
